summary: The change makes onSave async so it writes the whole store to data/notes.json after each save.

findings.title: Async onSave breaks the synchronous dispatch caller
findings.problem: onSave now returns a Promise, but dispatch in src/router.js:7 returns it unchanged. The handler in src/main.js:9 then passes that Promise straight to res.end.
findings.consequence: Node's res.end throws a TypeError for a Promise argument, so every POST /save request crashes the server. A failed writeFile rejection also goes unhandled, and newer Node versions terminate the process on it.
findings.fix: Make dispatch and the request handler await the result. Add a catch that answers with an error status.

findings.title: New snapshot write has no covering test
findings.problem: onSave now writes a file and returns a Promise. No test covers this new behaviour.
findings.consequence: A test that saved once through the router would have caught the crash. Without tests, later regressions in saving will also go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add a test that saves an id through dispatch. It should check the response text and the contents of the snapshot file.
